agree.reason: The 3 a.m. solo shift and the self-taught mastitis detection make a strong case, but the letter has no farm name, no signer name, no surname for Tomás and no contact details, so a hurried committee member can't verify it and may discount it.

honest.reason: Several claims go beyond the brief: 'nobody required him,' 'learned it on his own,' 'seriously ill,' 'went straight back to the 3 a.m. shift' and 'without reservation' all add strength the facts don't supply.

works_the_facts.reason: The letter never works out that 2 missed shifts in about 780 is roughly a 99.7% attendance rate, never puts a value on the nine mastitis catches (such as the $8,000 the vet estimated), and turns the attendance record into the muddled line 'two shifts... the one exception.'

right_comparison.reason: It says he 'already does part of the job your graduates are trained for,' but it never sets him clearly against a typical applicant or a typical worker on the crew.

qualification.reason: The writing-English caveat rests on a night class with no level, start date or progress, so the committee can't check it; the safety test that he failed once and then passed, which would show improvement, is not used.

objections.reason: It deals with the English weakness and the five-week absence, but it states the two-day notice without saying that he arranged his cousin to cover his shifts and came back on the date he gave, so the reader is left with a reliability doubt the facts would answer.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter in the right register, but it is signed only 'Farm Manager,' with no name, farm or phone number, which a reference letter needs.
